reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E1 discusses RHEAs generally but is truncated and does not mention laser cladding or specific microstructures. E2 and E3 describe laser cladding of non-refractory (TiAlCuNi) coatings on TC4, not refractory HEA coatings, and do not address BCC-rich microstructures, bonding quality, or preservation of bulk properties. The premises are therefore largely unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Laser cladding can produce a dense, low-porosity refractory HEA coating on TC4
The refractory HEA coating will form a fine-grained, BCC-rich microstructure
The coating will form a strong metallurgical bond with the TC4 substrate
The BCC-rich microstructure provides dispersion and solid solution strengthening, enhancing hardness and wear resistance
The coating will preserve the intrinsic light weight and strength of TC4
